problem.h2: Why an alternative to Pepper gets searched for
problem.lead: Pepper, from Pomegranate Technologies, sells an AI-first platform to independent distributors: a storefront, an Order Agent for order entry, and hubs for sales, finance, pricing and marketing. It is a lot of product, and most of it earns its place. What sends a buyer to look at a Pepper competitor is usually far narrower than the platform.

cards.h3: The phone accounts are still phoning
cards.body: A storefront only helps the kitchens that open it. The rest keep calling, texting and leaving voicemails at the end of a shift, and those are the orders your desk still writes up by hand.

cards.h3: On the Order Agent path, you do the checking
cards.body: Order Agent reads the voicemail, text, photo or PDF the kitchen already sent. Pepper's own product page describes no step where the kitchen confirms what was read, so your order desk is the first person to see it written down.

cards.h3: One more rollout is the last thing you need
cards.body: Pepper publishes 35 to 90 days for a typical go-live, across five phases, with an implementation manager and a deployed engineer assigned. Fair for a platform that size. Going through anything like it again for one channel is not, and no Pepper alternative should ask you to.

cards.h2: What Pepper keeps and what the voice step adds
cards.lead: VoiceOrder Solutions is no Pepper replacement, and it is not trying to be one. Nothing has to come out for it to go in, so the platform you rolled out stays exactly where it is.

items.h3: Keep the storefront, add the voice
items.body: Some accounts are never going to browse a catalog. They will talk instead, late in the evening, from the walk-in. The storefront stays for the ones who tap, and our app picks up the ones who talk.

items.h3: Try it on the accounts still calling
items.body: It goes in beside Pepper without a project, so you can start with the handful of accounts that never adopted the storefront and judge it on those before deciding anything bigger.

items.h3: The ERP keeps being the one destination
items.body: Both feed the system you have, so adding our app does not change where an order ends up. It arrives over EDI, the API or QuickBooks into the system your people already use, or by email as a file.

faq.h2: Questions from distributors who are keeping Pepper

items.q: Do we need a Pepper alternative so kitchens can check their own spoken orders?
items.a: No. Pepper can stay as it is, Order Agent included, while we add an app where kitchens say what they need and check every item themselves. The ones already ordering on Pepper's storefront carry on there. Nothing has to be switched off to try it.

items.q: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than Pepper?
items.a: Not at running the whole business on one platform: storefront, reps, collections and pricing. Pepper is built wide for that, and we are not trying to be. Where we help is narrower: a reorder your account speaks and signs off, and plenty of people looking for a Pepper alternative turn out to want exactly that one thing.

items.q: Is there a link between VoiceOrder Solutions and Pepper?
items.a: None. We have no connection to Pepper and no shared support arrangement. Each product hands its orders to your own system separately, ours by email with a file attached, over EDI or the API, or into QuickBooks. When ours go in by a direct feed, both land in the same system; by email, ours arrive as a file your team opens like any other.

items.q: Will our accounts be juggling Pepper's storefront and your app?
items.a: They should not have to. Kitchens already ordering through the storefront can stay on it. Offer our app to the ones who still call, text or leave a voicemail, because those orders cost your desk the most time. Anyone who keeps calling is handled as now, with no order number from us, since numbers come only with what our app sends.

items.q: How quickly can we actually be taking orders?
items.a: Most distributors reach that point in a day or two, and most of their customers send a first order the same day. There is no IT project and Pepper runs throughout, which is a very different job from the window Pepper publishes for standing up its whole platform.

We quote by distributor, so tell us about your operation and we will price it. Pepper quotes too and publishes no rate card. Since you would be keeping Pepper, the figure worth asking for is what our app adds on top.

items.q: Do our customers need new hardware or a tablet?
items.a: No. Our app runs on the iOS or Android phone already in their pocket. We send nothing out, there is nothing to bolt to a counter, and no device for you to support.

items.q: Where do the Pepper details on this page come from?
items.a: Pepper's own website. The module list, the storefront and Order Agent descriptions and the implementation window were all read off usepepper.com on 10 October 2026, including their own post on how long an implementation takes. We have not repeated their marketing numbers here. If any of it has changed since, this page is the thing that is out of date, not them.
